ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the side length of square $ABCD$ is $4$. Diagonal $AC$, points $E$, $F$ are respectively on the extensions of $BC$, $CD$, with $CE=2$, $DF=1$. Point $G$ is the midpoint of $EF$. Connect $OE$ and intersect $CD$ at point $H$. What is the length of $GH$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw OM$\perp$BC at M through point O, and draw GN$\perp$CF at N through point G,\\
since square ABCD,\\
thus CO=OA, and $\angle$ABC$=90^\circ$,\\
thus OM$\parallel$AB,\\
$\triangle$COM$\sim$$\triangle$CAB,\\
thus $\frac{CO}{AC}=\frac{OM}{AB}=\frac{CM}{BC}$ that is $\frac{CO}{2OC}=\frac{OM}{4}=\frac{CM}{BC}=\frac{1}{2}$,\\
we find OM=2 and CM=$\frac{1}{2}BC=\frac{1}{2}\times 4=2$,\\
since CE=2,\\
thus MC=CE=2, ME=MC+CE=4,\\
since CH$\parallel$AB,\\
thus CH$\parallel$OM,\\
thus $\frac{CH}{OM}=\frac{CE}{ME}$ that means $\frac{CH}{2}=\frac{2}{4}=\frac{1}{2}$,\\
thus CH=1,\\
since GN$\perp$CF, and $\angle$FCE$=90^\circ$,\\
thus GN$\parallel$CE and point G is the midpoint of EF,\\
thus $\triangle$FGN$\sim$$\triangle$FEC,\\
thus $\frac{FN}{FC}=\frac{NG}{CE}=\frac{FG}{FE}$ that means $\frac{FN}{FC}=\frac{NG}{CE}=\frac{FG}{2FG}=\frac{1}{2}$,\\
since DF=1,\\
thus CF=CD+DF=4+1=5,\\
thus $\frac{FN}{5}=\frac{NG}{2}=\frac{1}{2}$,\\
we find FN=2.5, NG=1,\\
thus NH=CF−FN−CH=5−2.5−1=1.5,\\
In right $\triangle$NHG, GH=$\sqrt{NG^{2}+NH^{2}}=\sqrt{1^{2}+1.5^{2}}=\boxed{\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{13}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is square ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, D is at the upper right; BC is extended to the right to E, CD is extended upward to F; the diagonals of the square intersect at O; line segment OE intersects CD at H; G is located on EF, is the midpoint of EF, and GH is connected. Solve by the coordinate method: take C as the origin, BC horizontally to the left, CD vertically upward, then C=(0,0), B=(-4,0), D=(0,4), A=(-4,4). The center O of the square is the intersection point of the diagonals, so O=(-2,2). Because CE=2 and E is on the extension line of BC, E=(2,0). Because DF=1 and F is on the extension line of CD, F=(0,5). G is the midpoint of EF, therefore G=((2+0)/2,(0+5)/2)=(1,5/2). The slope of line OE is (0-2)/(2-(-2))=-1/2, and its equation is y=1-x/2. When it intersects CD, x=0, so H=(0,1). Thus GH=sqrt((1-0)^2+(5/2-1)^2)=sqrt(1+9/4)=sqrt(13)/2.
